mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, thereby driving negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 YoY < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% for two consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for S&P 500 constituents and predicts negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during INDPRO 3-month decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which is expected to drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) move in opposite directions for three consecutive months, it signals monetary policy misalignment, which historically precedes market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL move in opposite direction for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of monetary policy misalignment.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of strong PAYEMS acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) over three months suggests households are saving more while facing rising prices, which typically foreshadows a future pullback in consumption and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and CPIAUCSL both rise for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both RSAFS and CPIAUCSL rise for three months.
